$comment: The SINGLE source of truth for what a remote-vault host string means to reach — rejected or accepted — across all three places that judge it: Rust `base_url` (src-tauri/src/remote_client.rs), the browser mock's `remoteMockError` (src/mocks/tauri-core.ts), and TS's pre-flight `hostFieldProblem` (src/document/remote-host-field.ts). Each of the three implements this same rule independently (different languages, no shared code) — that's the drift risk. This table is what pins them together: tests/remote-host-truth-table.test.ts checks every row against BOTH TS surfaces (mock + hostFieldProblem) and fails loudly the moment either diverges from this table. The Rust side has its own cargo tests asserting the exact same rows (remote_client.rs's `#[cfg(test)]` module) — if you change what any ONE of the three accepts/rejects, update this table AND the Rust test data in the same change, or the two suites silently drift again. `defaultPort`/`sharePortRows`/the SSH `share-port` rows below tie together the same three places by the same principle (Rust `DEFAULT_PORT`/`parse_ssh_host`/`validate_share_port` ⇄ TS `DEFAULT_SHARE_PORT`/`sshHostSuffixProblem`/`sharePortProblem` ⇄ mock `remote_share_start`/`remote_ssh_connect`/`remoteMockError`).
